To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
breast weight is associated to hormone receptors in breast cancer patients.
breast weight is associated to the risk of ER+ breast cancer.

1) high breast weight is a risk factor for ER+ breast cancer; 2) the risk of ER+ breast cancer increases with increasing breast weight; 3) the risk of breast cancer increases with breast weight in women with a family history of breast cancer, but not in women without a family history of the disease; 4) the risk of postmenopausal breast cancer is higher in women with high breast weight than in those with low breast weight.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of aromatase in breast cancer, and the relationship between breast weight and breast cancer.
the role of aromatase in breast cancer, and in particular with the role of the enzyme in the breast and in peripheral tissues.
the relationship between breast weight and the hormone receptor status of tumours.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

breast weight and hormone receptor (ER, PR and HER2) status are not related in women with breast tumours, but that there is a trend for ER+ tumours to be more common in women with higher BMI and breast weight.
the association of breast weight with breast cancer risk and ER status is unclear and requires further study.
there is no evidence that breast size is associated with breast cancer risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no evidence for an association between breast weight and breast cancer risk, and there is no evidence that breast weight is associated to ER status of the tumours.
there is no association between breast weight and ER+ status in women with invasive breast cancer.
there is a strong relationship between high breast weight and ER+ breast cancer, and that the aromatase inhibitor anastrazole reduces breast weight in postmenopauseal women with ER+ tumour.
The main takeaway from our work is that
breast weight is associated to ER+ breast cancer and that aromatase activity may be a contributing factor to this association.
women who have a higher breast weight are more likely to have a hormone receptor positive breast cancer.
breast weight is associated independently with ER+ breast cancer.
